steps: Scarce describes something in short supply, so it is hard to find.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: hard to find.
Cautious describes someone avoiding danger by being careful.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: careful.
Ancient means very old; modern refers to recent times.
The question asks for an opposite, not a synonym. Ancient contrasts with modern.
Climbing a steep trail takes effort, leaving hikers very tired.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: very tired.
Carrying glass with both hands protects it from breaking; fragile means easily broken.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: fragile.
A prediction is a statement about what may happen later.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: tell what may happen.
Enormous, huge, gigantic, and massive all describe great size.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: massive.
A silent ceremony suggests a serious, respectful mood.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: serious.
Improve means to make better.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: improve.
A reluctant person does not want to do something.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: unwilling.
Expand means get bigger; shrink means get smaller.
The question asks for an opposite, not a synonym. Expand contrasts with shrink.
Precise measurements are exact rather than approximate.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: exact.
Greeting every visitor suggests a friendly puppy.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: friendly.
A consequence follows from an action: it is a result.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: a result.
Inspect means look at something carefully and closely.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: inspect.
Frequent events occur often.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: happening often.
Permit means allow; forbid means not allow.
The question asks for an opposite, not a synonym. Permit contrasts with forbid.
An empty cabin left for years has been abandoned.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: left behind.
When everyone knows what to do, the directions are clear.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: clear.
Essential things are needed, or necessary.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: necessary.
Whispering, murmuring, and muttering are ways of speaking quietly.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: speak softly.
Swift describes quick movement, so a swift current moves fast.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: fast.
A strategy is a plan of actions to reach a goal.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: strategy.
Things that resemble each other look alike.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: look like.
Ordinary means usual; remarkable means unusual enough to notice.
The question asks for an opposite, not a synonym. Ordinary contrasts with remarkable.
Applause suggests the audience found the performance very impressive.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: very impressive.
Accurate passing requires attention; focus means direct your attention.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: focus.
Diminish means become smaller or decrease.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: decrease.
A reliable person or thing can be depended on.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: reliable.
A brief summary is short rather than lengthy.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: short.
Generous means willing to give; selfish means mainly concerned with oneself.
The question asks for an opposite, not a synonym. Generous contrasts with selfish.
Distribute means give things out among people or places.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: give out to several people.
Branches in the way stop hikers: the path is blocked.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: blocked.
Evident means plain to see or obvious.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: obvious.
Prevent means stop something before it happens.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: prevent.
A bridge that stays steady in wind is stable.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: steady.
Including every important step makes an explanation complete and thorough.
Choose the option that keeps that meaning: thorough.
Lena starts alone, but neighbors join her.
The ending shows people sharing food and stories: the idea brought them together.
Mr. Ortiz says a sign cannot grow tomatoes before he helps.
His remark shows doubt that Lena's plan will work.
Find Lena's sign near the beginning.
The rake, garden beds, and harvest all come later.
A sign cannot literally grow an idea.
Here, grow means encourage an idea to spread and inspire action.
The frost and rabbits damage the first crops.
The neighbors replant instead of quitting; this proves persistence.
At first the lot has weeds and wrappers.
At the end neighbors share tomatoes, baskets, and stories: food and friendship.
The passage explains roots, nutrients, and planned burns.
These details support the purpose of explaining how managed fire can help prairies.
Look for where grasses keep living tissue.
Their roots are below ground, away from the fast surface fire.
The passage says repeated fires stop many young trees.
Without fire, trees and shrubs may spread and turn prairie into woodland.
Managers prepare firebreaks and position crews with water.
These preparations help limit fire spread and respond to trouble.
The burn is chosen for a specific area and time.
That context makes prescribed mean planned and directed.
The final paragraph describes both disaster and preservation.
The effect depends on the place, conditions, and management.
The last line says wheels repeat, repeat.
That repeated wording points to the turning wheels' sound.
Notice sleeping farms, moonlight, and a child watching stars.
These quiet observations support a peaceful, thoughtful mood.
Farms do not literally sleep or fold.
The image describes farms that are quiet and hidden by nighttime darkness.
The train is moving while the child watches.
The porch light and tower are brief sights that pass the window.
Personification gives a nonhuman thing a human action.
Writing is a human action given to the train.
The instructions state why stones go in the bottom.
Their weight helps keep the bottle from tipping over.
The stones are covered with starting water.
Mark zero at that water surface so later rises measure rain only.
The cut-off top is turned upside down.
Its wide opening collects rain and its narrow opening channels it into the bottle.
Trees and roofs can intercept rain or shed extra water.
An open area gives a more representative rainfall measurement.
Read the sequence after recording the amount.
Empty extra water back to zero before setting the gauge outside again.
Eli draws the fork east rather than west.
That would send travelers the wrong way.
Eli notices an inaccurate route and stops printing.
Correcting the maps matters more to him than meeting the deadline.
Paper can be replaced, but a customer may stop trusting a printer.
The uncle means a damaged reputation is harder to repair.
Eli admits his error and shows the spoiled maps.
Admitting a mistake instead of hiding it demonstrates honesty.
Years later, the merchant becomes Eli's customer.
That later choice shows a lasting benefit of Eli's honesty.
Eli tells the truth even though the maps arrive late.
The merchant later trusts him with business, supporting the theme of honesty building trust.
The passage describes pest control, seeds, and pollination.
It also lists threats, so a main idea must include benefits and threats.
Fruit-eating bats carry fruit and release seeds elsewhere.
Those seeds can grow into plants in new places.
The passage says bats depend on healthy habitats.
A sudden decline can therefore signal problems in those habitats.
A shelter is a place where an animal lives or rests.
Protecting caves directly protects such a place for bats.
The passage says bats eat moths and beetles.
Eating crop pests can help farming.
Look in the first paragraph at how books were purchased.
Members' fees paid for the shared collection.
Subscription libraries charged membership fees.
Public libraries used community support and opened access to residents more broadly.
A building alone cannot run a library.
Paying staff and maintenance helps keep it operating over time.
Compare the original shared books with modern digital materials.
Both provide people access to information.
The passage moves from early collections to 1731, the 1800s, and modern libraries.
An account organized through time uses chronological order.
Passage A describes lessons; Passage B calls a garden useful.
Both agree a garden could benefit students.
Passage A proposes using the courtyard.
Passage B proposes two small raised boxes first: the disagreement is starting size.
Passage A names science, math, and language arts activities.
Those examples support using the garden for several school subjects.
Passage B mentions summer watering, tools, soil, and fencing.
These are concerns about cost and ongoing maintenance.
Keep Passage A's learning goal and Passage B's manageable start.
Begin with a small garden and expand after it succeeds.
The paragraph describes a science museum trip.
Sentence 3 about pizza does not support that topic.
Sentence 2 describes the first room visited.
First introduces the start of the visit's sequence.
Precise writing names who acted and what happened.
Museum educator and spinning column of air in a clear chamber give specific details.
Sentence 2 introduces fossils.
A guide explaining what bones reveal develops that same idea.
A conclusion should connect back to the museum's effect on learning.
Hoping to investigate like museum scientists brings the paragraph's ideas together.
Keep both facts: a dog was wandering and it wore a red collar.
Place with a red collar beside dog so the description attaches to the right noun.
Maya moves slowly so she will not frighten the dog.
Moved closer to keeps the meaning of approached without adding rushing or shouting.
Sentence 4 mentions a phone number and sentence 5 the owner's arrival.
Calling the number explains the missing connection.
Maya approaches the dog before reading its tag.
After the dog came near gives a logical time connection.
Maya carefully helps a lost dog find its owner.
A Responsible Choice describes her actions across the paragraph.
The topic is ways to save water.
Water is wet gives no useful way to save it, so remove sentence 5.
Sentence 2 presents leaking as a problem.
Sentence 3 follows with fixing leaks as the solution; keep that order.
A supporting example must show another way to save water.
Shorter showers reduce the time water runs.
Fixing leaks is one useful action.
Another useful habit introduces a second action with the same purpose.
The conclusion should explain the effect of the habits.
Small daily choices adding up to savings makes that connection specific.
Keep the audience becoming quiet, the curtain opening, and the narrator's feeling.
When links those events without changing who feels nervous.
Sentence 1 says the band practiced.
Repeating a difficult ending gives a concrete example of that practice.
The narrator is nervous at first but later stops shaking.
However signals this contrast.
In a concert, a band plays a musical piece.
Performed is the precise musical verb among the choices.
The paragraph moves from practice to nerves to a successful finish.
The central idea should connect all three.
Each is a singular subject, even with players after it.
Change have to has in line B: Each of the players has a water bottle.
The people doing the carrying need subject pronouns.
Change Marcus and me to Marcus and I in line A.
The kite is the subject and flew is a correct past-tense verb.
Higher than correctly compares its height with the other kites; no correction is needed.
Yesterday requires the simple past tense.
Change we seen to we saw in line A; seen needs a helper such as have.
It's means it is or it has.
Ownership needs its: the puppy wagged its tail. Correct line B.
Neither is singular here.
Change seem to seems in line B to agree with Neither.
Had already eaten describes an action completed before another past action.
When Dad brought gives that later action; the sentence is correct.
The word describes how the guide spoke, so use an adverb.
Change clear to clearly in line B.
The comparison is between two cousins.
Use taller for two, not tallest; correct line B.
The subject is three books, which is plural.
Change There is to There are in line A.
This imagines an unreal situation.
Use If I were the team captain in line A.
Class is treated as one group here.
Its correctly shows that the project belongs to the class; no correction is needed.
The people planting are the subject.
Replace Her with She in line A: She and Keisha planted.
The word describes how the storm moved.
Use the adverb quickly: more quickly than, in line B.
Shortest already expresses the superlative.
Remove most in line B; use the shortest.
The subject is basket, not apples.
A singular basket was sitting; change were to was in line B.
Carefully correctly describes measured.
Before he cut it gives a clear sequence; there is no error.
The snacks are distributed across a group of five students.
For this group distribution, use among all five students in line B.
Had brought correctly describes an action before the teacher asked.
Whether correctly introduces the indirect question; no error is needed.
Difficult needs more for a comparison.
Use more difficult than, not difficulter than, in line B.
Read places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands.
The 7 is in the ten-thousands place: 7 × 10,000 = 70,000.
Compare digits from left to right.
398,765 beats 389,765 in the thousands and beats the other 398,... choices in the hundreds or tens.

Installed seats add to the old total.
Subtract shipped boxes from the starting supply.
Split 24 into 20 + 4.
Equal groups mean multiplication.
Divide the total equally among nine buses.
9 × 40 = 360, leaving 72; 9 × 8 = 72, so each bus has 48.
There are no parentheses.
Do multiplication before addition, so evaluate 6 × 4 first.
Start inside parentheses: 12 − 8 = 4.
Then 3 × 4 = 12; finally 7 + 12 = 19.
A factor divides 42 with no remainder.
42 ÷ 6 = 7, so 6 is a factor.
A prime has exactly two positive factors: 1 and itself.
21 = 3 × 7, 27 = 3 × 9, and 33 = 3 × 11; 29 has no other positive factors.
Multiples of 4 begin 4, 8, 12; multiples of 6 begin 6, 12.
The first shared multiple is 12.
Find consecutive differences: 11 − 5 = 6 and 17 − 11 = 6.
23 − 17 is also 6, so add 6 each time.
Replace n with 8.
A number is represented by n; decreased by 12 means subtract 12.
Equals 35 gives n − 12 = 35.
Three books cost 3 × $14 = $42.
Add the $6 notebook: $42 + $6 = $48.
1,275 − 1,272 = 3 remain, fewer than the 8 needed for another full bag.
Multiply numerator and denominator by the same number.
24/48 is greatest, so choose 1/2.
Rename 3/4 as 6/8.
6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8; the denominator stays 8.
Use denominator 12: 5/6 = 10/12 and 1/4 = 3/12.
Rename 1/3 as 2/6; add whole parts: 2 + 1 = 3.
Four groups of 2/3 make (4 × 2)/3 = 8/3.
8 ÷ 3 is 2 remainder 2, so 8/3 = 2 2/3.
Three batches need three groups of 3/4 cup.
Rename 2/5 mile as 4/10 mile.
Each meter contains four quarter-meter pieces.
Five meters contain 5 × 4 = 20 pieces.
Equivalent fractions multiply both parts by the same number.
7/10 × 2/2 = 14/20; the other inequalities reverse the actual order.
Halfway means two equal parts of the interval.
One of those two parts is 1/2.
Both amounts are in eighths: 7/8 − 3/8 = 4/8.
Divide numerator and denominator by 4: 4/8 = 1/2.
One whole contains five fifths.
Three wholes contain 3 × 5 fifths, so dividing by 1/5 is multiplying by 5.
Rename 2 1/2 as 2 2/4.
Line up decimal places: 3.8 = 3.80.
Write 12.5 as 12.50 and subtract matching places.
Multiplying by 10 makes every digit worth ten times as much.
6 ones become 6 tens and 4 tenths become 4 ones: 64.
0.37 is 37 hundredths.
37 × 6 = 222 hundredths = 2.22.
Write 3.6 as 3.60 and line up decimal places.
The first place after the decimal is tenths.
Seven tenths is written 0.7.
Write the choices with equal places: 4.090, 4.900, 4.190, 4.099.
All have 4 ones; 9 tenths is largest, so 4.9 wins.
The hundredths digit is 4 and the next digit is 6.
Because 6 ≥ 5, increase the hundredths to 5: 18.75.
Multiply the price by four notebooks.
Start with 5.00 liters and subtract 1.86.
Area of a rectangle is length × width.
12 × 7 = 84 square centimeters.
Perimeter is 2 × (length + width), so length + width = 30 ÷ 2 = 15.
Width = 15 − 9 = 6 meters.
Volume is length × width × height.
5 × 3 = 15 per layer; 15 × 4 = 60 cubic units.
Volume measures three-dimensional space, so use cubic units.
A room is large enough that cubic meters are appropriate.
A right angle is 90° and a straight angle is 180°.
125° is between them, so it is obtuse.
A rectangle guarantees four right angles; a rhombus guarantees four equal sides.
A square guarantees both properties.
Both points have x = 2, so measure the vertical difference.
9 − 5 = 4 units.
One foot is 12 inches.
3 × 12 = 36 inches.
Ben read 9 and Cara read 5.
How many more means subtract: 9 − 5 = 4.
Mode means the value occurring most often.
6 occurs twice; each other number occurs once.
There are 3 + 5 + 2 = 10 marbles, including 2 green.
Probability = 2/10 = 1/5.
At least 3 includes 3 and anything greater.
Count 3, 3, 3, 4, 5: five measurements.
Each time x rises by 1, y rises by 3.
3 × 1 + 1 = 4; the rule y = 3x + 1 also gives 7, 10, and 13.
Add the daily sales.
Add 1 hour to 6:35 p.m. to reach 7:35.
Add 25 minutes to 8:00, then the remaining 23 minutes: 8:23 p.m.
Identify the cause being tested: sunlight.
Change only the amount of sunlight while keeping other growing conditions alike.
A single result might reflect a mistake or chance.
Repeating trials checks whether the result is consistent and more reliable.
Volume is the amount of space the water occupies.
A graduated cylinder has marked volume units for reading liquid amounts.
An observation is something measured or directly noticed.
Growing 2 cm is a measured result, rather than a prediction or explanation.
Time changes in a sequence from day to day.
A line graph connects the temperatures to show that trend.
Different methods or measurements can produce different results.
Compare those first before deciding what the experiment shows.
A hypothesis makes a prediction that measurements can check.
Light amount and plant height over two weeks can both be measured.
Water enters through the roots and must move upward.
The stem contains tissue that carries water toward the leaves.
Flowers contain reproductive structures.
They help plants make seeds, often after pollination.
A producer makes its own food using an energy source.
Grass uses sunlight to make food through photosynthesis.
Follow the chain from grasshopper to frog.
Frogs eat grasshoppers, so fewer grasshoppers means less frog food.
Dead organisms contain nutrients.
Decomposers break them down and return nutrients for reuse.
Inherited traits come through biological parents.
Natural hair texture is inherited; practiced skills are learned.
Arctic habitats are cold.
Thick fur traps insulating air and reduces loss of body heat.
Breathing brings air into the lungs.
The respiratory system transfers oxygen from that air into the body.
Food must be broken into smaller, usable substances.
That breakdown and nutrient absorption are digestive functions.
Seasons change temperature and food availability.
A bird migrating south in autumn changes its behavior with the season.
Compare solids, liquids, and gases.
A solid keeps both its shape and volume under ordinary conditions.
Ice is solid water.
Melting makes liquid water, so the change is solid to liquid.
A reversible change can be undone.
Frozen water can melt back into liquid water.
Both spoons can be at the same temperature.
Metal transfers heat out of your warmer hand faster, making it feel colder.
A conductor allows electric charge to flow easily.
Copper is a metal commonly used for conducting wire.
Electric current needs a complete path.
A closed circuit provides that path through the bulb.
Objects near Earth are attracted toward it.
This attractive force is gravity.
Friction opposes relative sliding between surfaces.
It commonly slows a moving object and transfers energy into heat.
Each current-carrying coil contributes a magnetic field.
With the same current, more turns around the nail strengthen the electromagnet.
Sound begins when something moves back and forth.
Those vibrations create waves through a material such as air.
A smooth shiny surface reflects light in an organized direction.
A mirror fits that description best.
Earth turns so a location faces the Sun and then faces away.
This rotation produces the cycle of day and night.
One orbit is one complete trip around the Sun.
Earth takes approximately one year to make that trip.
The Sun usually lights half the Moon.
As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different amounts of that lit half.
Liquid water can gain enough energy to enter the air as gas.
That liquid-to-gas process is evaporation.
Cooling water vapor can form tiny liquid droplets.
That change is condensation and can form clouds.
Temperature tells how warm or cold the air is.
A thermometer measures temperature.
Sediment settles in layers.
Pressure and natural cement can bind those layers into sedimentary rock.
Moving water, wind, or ice can carry rock material away.
This removal is erosion; weathering is the related breakdown of rock in place.
Fossils are preserved remains or traces of past life.
They give evidence of ancient organisms and their environments.
Map symbols stand for real features.
The legend explains what each symbol means.
A compass rose labels north, south, east, and west.
These labels show directions on a map.
The Equator is 0° latitude.
Latitude describes how far north or south a location is in degrees.
Look for both a flat top and high elevation above nearby land.
Those features describe a plateau.
People and businesses need water and ways to move goods.
Rivers provide water and transportation routes that support settlement and trade.
Renewable resources are replenished naturally.
Wind is renewed by atmospheric processes rather than used up like fossil fuel.
Very little precipitation limits plant growth.
Those dry conditions describe a desert.
A scale compares a map length with a real-world length.
Use it to convert a measured map distance into actual distance.
Adapting means adjusting to local conditions.
Raising houses on stilts helps people live with floodwater.
Density describes how many people live in an area.
A population density map shows concentrations of people.
Tenochtitlan was the capital of the Aztec Empire.
Its location was in what is now Mexico City.
Farming requires water and productive soil.
River valleys supplied water and often fertile soil for early settlements.
Renaissance means rebirth.
The period renewed interest in classical learning and supported art and science.
Printing could make many copies of a text.
The printing press spread written ideas faster than copying by hand.
European merchants wanted access to valuable goods.
Explorers sought new ocean trade routes.
The exchange connected the Americas with the Eastern Hemisphere.
Crops, animals, and diseases moved between them.
Colonists were taxed by Parliament.
They objected that they had no elected representatives there.
The Declaration discusses rights and consent of the governed.
Government authority should come from the people it governs.
The Articles of Confederation created a weak national government.
The convention met to address those weaknesses and produced a new Constitution.
The purchase added a vast territory west of the Mississippi.
It greatly expanded the country's land area.
Congress is the federal legislative branch.
Its role includes making laws.
Federal courts belong to the judicial branch.
They interpret and apply laws in cases.
Each branch has powers that limit the others.
These checks help prevent power from concentrating in one branch.
Rights are freedoms; responsibilities are duties.
Obeying laws is a civic responsibility.
The First Amendment protects several freedoms of expression and belief.
Freedom of speech is one of them.
Local needs include roads and emergency services.
Local governments organize and provide many of these services.
Voters express their choices on a ballot.
Those choices help select leaders or decide public issues.
A constitution defines government structure and basic authority.
It is a basic governing plan and set of rules.
A mayor is a municipal office.
Municipal government means city or town government.
Production creates goods or supplies services.
A producer is the person or business doing that work.
Consumption means using goods or services.
A consumer buys or uses them.
A good is a physical product; a service is work done for someone.
A haircut is work provided by a barber or stylist.
Resources cannot meet every possible want.
That limited availability compared with wants is scarcity.
More buyers want the same available quantity.
The increased competition to buy tends to raise price.
Saving sets money aside instead of spending it now.
The money can help meet future needs or goals.
Income is money coming in; spending is money going out.
A budget plans how those amounts will be managed.
Regions differ in resources and production strengths.
Trade can give each access to goods that others produce more efficiently.
